sentences.text: Hamititan is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur belonging to the unranked family Titanosauria.
Phylogenetic analysis places this animal as a derived non-lithostrotian titanosaur related to Epachthosaurus, Kaijutitan, and Notocolossus.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of only seven preserved tail vertebrae with three chevrons.
A theropod tooth found near the holotype suggests the dinosaur was preyed upon shortly after death.
A fossil site known as a Konservat-Lagerstätte was discovered in 2006 in the Hami region of Xinjiang, China.
The species name xinjiangensis refers to the Chinese province of Xinjiang.
Hamititan lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage, with a time range estimated between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
Contemporary fauna at the locality included the pterosaur Hamipterus and the sauropod Silutitan.
